lines.text: St. CIII.—मनोरथोपरचितप्रासाद is equivalent to castle in the air.
The Stanza occurs at p. 301 of the Kâvyasangraha.—S'ârdûla-
vikrîḍita.
St. CIV.—आघ्रान is apparently used as a synonyme of ग्रस्त oc-
curring in the fourth line. I observe that Râmarshi expressly
says ग्रस्तमित्यर्थः. The word is used in a similar sense in the Das'a-
kumâracharita p. 11 (Calc. Ed. 1925 Sam.) विद्युच्चलं यौवनम् it will be
seen breaks the symmetry of the Stanza, but none of the variants
preserve it. उपहता is a better reading than अपहृता. वा इति आश्चर्ये says
Râmarshi. But see our note to Nîtis'ataka St. 32.—S'ârdûla-
vikrîḍita.
St. CV.—आधिव्याधि may be taken as a Dvandva. In the Mâlatî-
Mâdhava (p. 145) where the expression occurs it is explained by
Jagaddhara as आधय एव व्याधयः; unnecessarily, I think. Construe यत्र
लक्ष्मीस्तत्र आपदः पतन्ति—आपद् is not a very usual form but occurs
in Mṛichchhakaṭika p. 213 (Calc. Ed.) आत्मसात्. See Siddh. Kaum.
I., 731. तत्किं नाम &c. “and what indeed is there which unbridled
destiny has created well-constituted.”—S'ârdûlavikrîḍita.
St. CVI.—नियमित = cramped, compressed. The second line as it
stands in our text is explained by both commentators, but it cer-
tainly seems to involve a pleonasm. “In youth which is painful
through separation there is separation.” The reading of Bo.
and N. would seem to be better. “The enjoyments of youth are
painful by reason of the grief of separation.” नारीणामप्यवज्ञा is taken
by the commentator with the second line and to this construc-
tion the two अपि would seem to give support. Râmarshi's read-
ing is somewhat different and he takes the whole line as one con-
struing असाधुः with अवज्ञा. This I think is better. See St. 111. As
it stands the first अपि may be taken as meaning again, and इत्यतः
or some expression of like import must be supplied after विलसति.
